definition: A graph-editor display mode (Blender's 'Normalize') that rescales every visible F-curve to fit the same +-1 vertical range regardless of its native unit, so channels measured in incompatible units — degrees of rotation, studs/meters of location, a dimensionless scale factor — can be read side by side on one screen without hunting for each channel's own value range.
purpose: Let a single glance compare the RELATIVE shape of several differently-scaled channels at once — steepness, number of extrema, symmetry — which the raw-unit view makes impractical because one channel's real range can dwarf another's on the same plot.
visible_effect: Every selected curve is force-fitted between +1 and -1; a location channel moving 0.3 studs and a rotation channel sweeping 340 degrees appear as comparably-sized waves instead of one being a flat line next to the other.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: not applicable — a pure authoring-view convenience with no effect on the finished, played-back motion.
physical_interpretation: none — the rescaling is a DISPLAY transform only; it never touches the stored keyed values, so nothing about the motion itself changes, only what is legible on screen.
use_cases: comparing the relative timing/shape of several channels of different units on the same held pose or action, e.g. is the rotation channel's peak velocity happening before or after the location channel's
a workspace setup step done once per file so every later session of curve-reading benefits, per the presenter's own framing
non_use_cases: reading an actual absolute value off a curve ("how many degrees is this key"), which the normalized view actively hides since every channel is rescaled to the same visual range
comparing two SEPARATE curves' real magnitude against each other, which normalization specifically defeats by design
interactions: No existing Cadence knowledge card names a curve-reading technique, since Cadence currently exposes no per-channel value-vs-time graph view for pose tracks to read this way in the first place (see cadence_representation).
cadence_representation: Not represented — Cadence's timeline (`renderer/js/timeline.js`) draws per-part keyframe positions on a shared frame axis, not a per-channel F-curve view, so there is currently no screen where two differently-scaled channels could even be overlaid to normalize. The VFX side has per-modifier curves (`vfx_get_curve`/`vfx_set_curve` exist as MCP tools) which is a closer analogue if a future curve view is ever built there; whether that surface already normalizes for display was not checked this session.
control_surface: None currently; would be a display toggle on any future per-channel curve view, not a mutation.
detection_and_measurement_methods: not measurable in this build — a display convention, not a property of the underlying keys `ai/motion.js` samples.
generation_or_modification_methods: not applicable — no generation step; a viewer preference only.
failure_modes: misreading a normalized curve's on-screen height as an absolute value instead of a relative shape, especially for a viewer unfamiliar with the convention
leaving normalize on while trying to eyeball an actual keyframe value, then hand-typing a wrong number because the view no longer shows true scale
roblox_considerations: None — a pure authoring-tool display convention independent of the runtime engine.
examples: the presenter overlays a tail rig's location, rotation and scale channels (three different units) at once with Normalize on, calling it 'very, very important' and something he 'always have on' as an animator (video @ 2:57-3:31)
the same presenter contrasts this against Normalize off, where finding a channel's own range takes 'a lot of scrolling up and down' — shown directly by his own on-screen struggle (video @ 3:18-3:29)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/vKgO3NsYORo @ 2:57-3:31 — BrianKouhi demonstrates Blender's graph editor Normalize option forcing every channel to fit the same +-1 range regardless of native unit, and contrasts it against Normalize-off requiring extensive scrolling to find a channel's own range; frames at t=03:38-04:07 show the resulting multi-colour overlaid curves (visible on screen through an unrelated sponsor-read segment at that timestamp, which is why the frame evidence and the transcript evidence cover different spans); experimental until validated
